bet: Combining the physically-motivated Monod/Gaussian structure of the current program (which captures saturation and optima) with normalized inputs from inspirations improves numerical conditioning for BFGS, while keeping the multiplicative environmental gating that better reflects biological reality than pure polynomial sums

Linear-in-parameters GAM with Legendre basis eliminates local minima that plague multiplicative models; BFGS converges to global optimum on a convex-like landscape, enabling better fit than the non-convex Monod-Gaussian model

RBF basis with fixed centers provides a smooth, non-linear function approximation that can capture complex interactions in the E. coli growth data better than a quadratic polynomial. The Gaussian basis functions allow local fitting of the response surface, and with 10 parameters as weights, BFGS should be able to optimize the weights effectively since the problem becomes linear in the parameters given fixed centers. This structural change from polynomial to RBF may better capture the non-linear dynamics of microbial growth.
